reason: In this passage from 2 Kings 22-23, regular people (הָעָם - the common folk) are portrayed positively when they appear. They are depicted as: (1) gathering obediently at the king's command to hear the Book of the Covenant, (2) participating faithfully in covenant-making "from smallest to greatest," (3) standing together in religious devotion with their leadership, and (4) making a responsible collective decision in choosing Jehoahaz as king after Josiah's death. While the narrative centers primarily on elite figures (the king, priests, and officials), the ordinary people who do appear in the text are shown as compliant, faithful, and making sound choices. There is no negative characterization of regular people in this account.
